uiDesignCheck.note: The scan covers apps/web only. Studio diff read by hand: one help sentence changed in AddFilesDialog (sentence case, no tokens, CSS or controls); the tray lists a kept layer once instead of twice. No blocking or design-system findings.

decisions: A ZIP of at most 16 MiB is retained unchanged by a new route POST /api/v1/ingestion/cases/{caseId}/intake/archives (profile zip-manual-v1, actor bound, case revision +1, idempotent by request key, deduplicated by hash). A larger ZIP keeps arriving through /uploads as large-original-v1.
Fan-out runs when the archive is enrolled (POST .../intake/items) and again on every later enrolment, which is the retry: members already kept are not kept twice.

A layer is a member the probe read as geojson without refusal. Each is read back from the retained ZIP in one-MiB ranges, inflated to at most 16 MiB, checked against the directory size and CRC-32, then retained through the existing GeoJSON retain (geojson-manual-v1, same inventory and processor inspection as a dropped file) with inspection.archiveMember = zip-layer/1 lineage: archive source id, revision, sha256, archive item id, member path, directory ordinal, sizes, CRC-32 and member sha256.
Every layer is retained before any is enrolled: a layer's draft creates packages, after which the GeoJSON retain refuses the case.

The member row under the archive names its child original (source_id). The child original has its own top-level item, so drafting, large-file and run code is unchanged; the Studio tray hides the member row of a kept layer.
At most 64 layers per archive, each at most 16 MiB; the rest stay in the archive with a limit reason (ZIP_LAYER_LIMIT, ZIP_LAYER_SIZE). A failed layer stores a code and fixed words only.
Identical bytes already retained in the case reuse that original (the existing hash deduplication); its receipt then carries no lineage, and the member row still names it.
The Studio reads a ZIP's central directory from its tail to route it: GeoJSON/JSON members and no .shp/.gpkg go to the batch; every other ZIP keeps direct import.
limits: No PostgreSQL, object store, processor or served HTTP walk was run; the processor inspection of each layer is the existing retain's and is stubbed in the tests.
Fan-out runs inside the enrol request; a ZIP with many large layers makes that request long. A job would remove that.
A batch case that already has drafted packages refuses new originals, archives and their layers included (existing rule of the GeoJSON retain).
ZIP64, encrypted, nested and non-UTF-8-named members are not kept; their reasons come from the existing ZIP guards.
